_synthetic: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. This file once held a live Whoop pull keyed to a real user_id. It was replaced before publication. Every user_id, cycle_id, sleep_id, timestamp and physiological value below is fabricated. The JSON shape, field names, nesting, float precision and value ranges match the real Whoop /recovery payload exactly, so the case still exercises the same parsing difficulty and still scores to the same verdict. Synthetic sleep_ids all begin with the marker 'fa4e'; the synthetic user_id begins with 999.
name: real_param_recovery
commitment: Hit recovery score 70 or higher on at least 3 days between April 13 and April 18 (6-day window).

expected.rationale: Synthetic Whoop-shaped recovery data, Apr 13-18 2026. Recovery scores in window: 54 (4/13 01:38Z), 12 (4/13 21:26Z - two cycles on the same calendar day; the late-evening one is the sleep assigned to the 4/13 IST evening), 78 (4/15), 26 (4/16), 63 (4/17), 47 (4/18). Only 1 day hit >= 70 (Apr 15 at 78). Threshold requires 3. Verdict: miss. Also note the two-cycles-on-Apr-13 pattern: Whoop creates a short extra cycle when the user goes to bed well after a nap, and a settlement oracle must decide whether to count the nap cycle or only the primary sleep cycle.
expected.trap: There are two cycles on Apr 13. A naive model may count sleep_id fa4e0003 (recovery 54) as 'Apr 13' and cycle 9000041004 (recovery 12) as 'Apr 14 morning' - but created_at is the assignment date, not the wake date. Oracle should clarify the counting rule. Apr 14 has no cycle at all.
